messages:
maria.sales: Hi team — AcmeCloud wants a short Dedicated POC. They operate from locked-down corporate VMs that only allow traffic to a handful of IPv4 addresses. Two asks: (A) can we surface a small set of static egress IPs for the Dedicated endpoint so their firewall can allowlist? (B) estimate for 1 GPU for 10 business days (dev + validation). Also they want a scoped API key and an expiry.

ash.runtime: We can support this. Options: (1) customer configures outbound NAT to our public endpoint (they allowlist our host / IPs); (2) Redwood-managed static egress pool attached to the Dedicated instance (we publish 21 IPv4 addresses); (3) Private/VPC option if they need peering. For quick POC, option (2) is fastest for the customer.

ravi.network: If we do Redwood-managed egress, we need to allocate dedicated NAT IPs in the region and document them. We'll also need the exact source IPs/CIDRs from the customer's side for troubleshooting (even though they only egress outbound). Note: if the customer's proxy performs TLS interception, they'll need to allow TLS passthrough.

liz.security: From security: we require the POC intake form and a signed short POC DPA/MSA for data handling. Provide SOC2 link and the standard questionnaire. For allowlist we need: (a) who is the technical contact, (b) approved outbound CIDRs, (c) whether they expect request/response logs to be stored, and (d) any compliance restrictions.

chris.billing: Pricing estimate: 1x A10-like GPU for 10 business days 1 assuming light test traffic 1 estimate $1,2001$2,000 (pro-rated dedicated hourly + model compute). Redwood-managed static egress add-on: $400/month (we can prorate to ~$501$100 for the POC). Scoped API key and 30% trial credit available. I'll confirm exact quote and produce a short line-item PDF.

maria.sales: Can someone draft a minimal "allowlist packet" with exact wording I can send to their infra team? Also need the curl example for their engineers and the expiry format for the POC key.

ash.runtime: Draft packet below — replace placeholder IPs with canonical values once Ravi posts them.

```
Allowlist packet (send to customer's infra/security):
- Service hostname: dedicated-us-east1.redwood.ai (TLS)
- Outbound IPs to allowlist (example): 52.11.101.45, 52.11.101.46
- Ports: TCP 443 outbound
- Purpose: Allow outbound requests from your app to Redwood Dedicated inference endpoint for 10-day POC
- Contact: maria.sales@redwood.ai (sales), ravi.network@redwood.ai (network), liz.security@redwood.ai (security)
- Notes: POC API key will be time-limited and scoped. Logs retained for POC: request/response metadata; bodies redacted by default unless customer opts in.

Firewall example (permit outbound):
- allow ip any host 52.11.101.45 eq 443

Sample curl (POC key placeholder):
curl -X POST https://dedicated-us-east1.redwood.ai/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer POC_KEY_EXPIRES_2026-04-15" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test prompt"}'
```

ravi.network: Confirming: I will provision a 2-ip egress pair in ENG-3098 and post the canonical /32s here by EOD. If they need IPv6 we need a separate ticket.

liz.security: Also attaching the intake URL: https://redwood.sharepoint/poc-intake. Requesting they complete it before we provision keys. We will redact PII in logs unless they sign the POC data opt-in.

infra-bot: Created ticket ENG-3098 for egress IP assignment and POC routing. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-3098

maria.sales: Great — I'll send this to AcmeCloud now and ask for the intake + their firewall ACL. Thanks all :rocket:
